claims.text: The proposed stepwise processing route can simultaneously increase yield strength and tensile ductility in a brittle multi-principal element alloy.
NbMoTaW is a brittle refractory multi-principal element alloy at room temperature.
Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 can exhibit severe tensile brittleness.
The relevant as-cast or conventionally treated alloys are characterized by coarse grains, grain-boundary precipitates, and low room-temperature ductility.
A high-temperature treatment at 900 °C for 5 minutes followed by aging at 650 °C for 20 hours is an effective stepwise processing schedule.
The rapid high-temperature anneal generates dislocation pile-ups.
Dislocation pile-ups enable rapid pipe diffusion.
Low-temperature aging nucleates nanoscale precipitates at dislocation sites within grain interiors.
The stepwise treatment avoids precipitation at grain boundaries.
Controlled cooling and aging suppress grain-boundary nucleation.
The treatment produces a homogeneous intragranular distribution of nanoscale δ-lamellae or γ″ particles.
Locating precipitates inside grains rather than at grain boundaries prevents intergranular embrittlement.
Two types of nanoscale precipitates provide synergistic precipitation strengthening.
The intragranular precipitates pin dislocations without compromising ductility.
Grain-boundary precipitates create weak paths for intergranular crack propagation.
Precipitation hardening increases yield strength while suppression of intergranular embrittlement increases tensile ductility.
The processed material can reach approximately 2.0 GPa yield strength and approximately 15% ductility, compared with approximately 600 MPa yield strength in the as-cast state.
Conventional long-duration annealing or standard aging promotes grain-boundary precipitation and consequent intergranular embrittlement.
The strategy is limited to alloys whose chemistry and diffusion kinetics permit formation of suitable δ-lamellae, γ″, or analogous strengthening precipitates through pipe diffusion.

The hypothesis is falsified if the stepwise-treated specimens show no significant ductility improvement despite homogeneous intragranular precipitation, or show intergranular fracture or lower ductility than the conventional-treatment control.

contradictions.description: The route is repeatedly called thermo-mechanical, but the specified intervention and comparison contain only annealing and aging, with no explicit deformation or other mechanical-processing step to create the required dislocation pile-ups.
